title: Even and Odd Components of the Symplectic Weil Representation
body_html:
Even and Odd Components of the Symplectic Weil Representation

Let \((E,j)\) be a symplectic vector space of dimension \(2\ell\) over a finite field \(k\) of odd order \(q\), and let \(W_\xi^{E,j}\) be the symplectic Weil representation attached to a nontrivial central character \(\xi\).

In a Schrodinger model attached to a Witt decomposition, the element \(-1\) separates functions into even and odd parts. The Weil representation splits into two simple components: \[ W_\xi^{E,j}=W_\xi^{E,j,+}\oplus W_\xi^{E,j,-}, \] with degrees \[ \deg W_\xi^{E,j,+}=\frac{q^\ell+1}{2}, \qquad \deg W_\xi^{E,j,-}=\frac{q^\ell-1}{2}. \]

The even component has Borel type. The odd component has the type corresponding to the long root.
